_readme: Surf breaks resolved by hand, for references the matching rules in
scripts/attest-surf-spots.mjs cannot resolve, or resolve to the wrong place.
Each entry is one reference name, per country, and one decision:
osm     the OpenStreetMap object that IS the break ("way/123"). Its
coordinate is published like any other OSM place; stage 1.6
(scripts/add-reviewed-places.mjs) adds it to the raw file if stage 1
absent  why the break has no OSM place of its own: a nickname for a peak
then publishes it at the coordinate surf-forecast's page prints.
why     what was checked: which beach the break is, and how that was known.
A decision replaces the rules for that reference in both directions: it
attests the place a person checked, and stops the rules attesting another.
Nothing here is a coordinate: a decision names an OSM object, or none.

Spain.why: The river-mouth peak at the west end of Barbate's town beach, which OSM names Playa del Carmen; the reference point is 0.7 km off it.
Misspelling of La Barrosa, Chiclana; OSM's Playa de La Barrosa.
La Barrosa, Chiclana. The polygon centroid sits 2 km from the reference because the beach is 8 km long.
La Playita is the local name of Playa de Santa María del Mar in Cádiz; the reference point is 0.2 km from it.
Town-named break: the reference point stands on Mojácar Playa's Playa de Vista de los Ángeles (0.1 km).
A peak by San José harbour, Cabo de Gata; OSM's Playa de San José is the beach it breaks off.
A peak at the south end of San José's beach, Cabo de Gata; OSM's Playa de San José (0.3 km).
